entities.summary: Jacob de Marchia, commonly known in English as Saint James of the Marches, was an Italian Friar Minor, preacher and writer. He was a Papal legate and Inquisitor of the Order of Preachers, with a strong emphasis on the importance of education and the dissemination of knowledge. This emphasis led to his involvement in the founding of the University of Bologna, one of the oldest continuously operating universities in the world. This marked a significant turning point in the history of higher education, as it established the model for the modern university and paved the way for the development of institutions such as Oxford and Cambridge. The impact of this institution can still be seen today, with the University of Bologna remaining a leading center of learning in Italy and Europe. The spread of knowledge and education during this period was a key factor in the Renaissance, which saw a resurgence of interest in classical learning and the arts. This, in turn, contributed to the cultural and scientific developments of the 16th and 17th centuries, including the emergence of modern science and the rise of nation-states. The legacy of James of the Marches can be seen in the many institutions of higher learning that he helped to establish, and in the ongoing importance of education as a driving force for social and cultural change.
